issues.failure_explanation: Linearity and Gaussian noises do not make a non-Gaussian prior Gaussian. For example, with a scalar two-point prior and a linear observation with Gaussian noise, the Bayesian posterior remains supported on those two points, whereas the perturbed-observation EnKF update generally does not. The paper permits a general prior but asserts exact Bayesian convergence without the additional initial-law hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: For linear systems with Gaussian noise, the EnKF provides a Monte Carlo approximation of the classical Kalman filter and converges to the exact Bayesian solution as the ensemble size increases.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require a Gaussian initial distribution, together with the usual independence assumptions, in the exact-Bayesian convergence statement.
issues.overall_effect: The introductory exactness claim is broader than the valid linear-Gaussian filtering regime.
issues.title: Exact Bayesian convergence also requires a Gaussian initial law
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local hypothesis correction that preserves the intended linear-Gaussian result and the proposed method.

issues.failure_explanation: The physical model includes fresh process noise, but neither the latent transition nor the forecast introduces its transformed uncertainty. Even with identity encoders and an exactly linear physical model, the algorithm predicts covariance A P Aᵀ instead of A P Aᵀ+Q. Thus this discrepancy survives perfect learning and an infinite ensemble; it is not a nonlinear approximation error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict the claimed filtering formulation explicitly to Q_k=0, or specify a latent transition-error model and propagate its noise and covariance. The source supplies no construction for the latter.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm is not an EnKF reformulation of the stated stochastic forward model when Q is nonzero, and its forecast uncertainty can collapse despite continuing process uncertainty.
issues.title: The latent forecast drops the stated process uncertainty
issues.why_classification: The source-supported restriction removes the stated nonzero-process-noise regime; retaining that regime requires an additional stochastic latent-model construction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In practice, a convenient and commonly used choice is $\mathbf{H} = \mathbf{I}$, in which case the observation encoder directly maps measurements into the latent state space without introducing additional trainable parameters.

issues.failure_explanation: Squared-error alignment learns a conditional mean, not a state-conditional additive Gaussian observation channel with the prescribed H. For example, take independent X and η distributed as N(0,1), Y=X+η, E=identity, and H=1. The population alignment minimizer is E_obs(Y)=Y/2. Its residual relative to X is (η−X)/2, whose conditional mean given X is −X/2. It therefore does not satisfy the observation model used by the gain, even in this linear-Gaussian example. No noise-law or covariance calibration correcting this is supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the guaranteed latent-model consistency and describe this as a heuristic observation surrogate, or introduce and justify a state-conditional observation/noise calibration with a corresponding filtering update.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted structural consistency of the latent analysis step does not follow from the training construction; the update can use an incorrect conditional mean and noise model.
issues.title: Observation alignment does not produce the assumed measurement likelihood
issues.why_classification: The available weakening abandons a central structural guarantee. Preserving that guarantee requires a statistical construction not present in the source.

issues.failure_explanation: The estimator is defined by minimizing a softly penalized objective over a trainable matrix, not by minimizing over the hard norm ball introduced in the appendix. A finite penalty does not establish membership in that ball. In particular, the bound on the true A-star does not imply the same bound on the learned matrix. Thus both the zero-regularizer assertion and the restriction of the estimator to the covered linear class are unjustified.

The proof supplies no uniform argument accounting for this second learned occurrence of E.

issues.failure_explanation: Even granting that the asserted observation-to-latent map exists, Assumption 1 controls the state manifold, not the observation domain or that map's regularity. No hypothesis bounds the observation operator, its inverse on the support, or the fixed encoder's relevant Lipschitz constants. Arbitrary identifiable observation reparameterizations can make the target arbitrarily irregular while the listed constants remain unchanged. The bounded-input, n-dimensional approximation argument therefore cannot simply be transferred by replacing D with D_y.

issues.failure_explanation: Successive windows share observations already assimilated into the forecast distribution. Consequently their encoded errors are generally temporally correlated and correlated with the forecast error. This occurs even for affine encoders and Gaussian sensor noises: averaging two successive scalar noises gives adjacent encoded-noise covariance σ²/4. Using the ordinary unchanged Kalman update can therefore count old measurements again without the required conditional or cross-covariance correction.

failure_location.quote: This approach allows the latent observation embedding to exploit short-term temporal correlations without modifying the filtering formulation.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the claim that delay embedding preserves the ordinary innovation model. Either retain L=1 for that formulation or derive a conditional/augmented update that accounts for reused observations and their cross-covariances.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed statistically unchanged extension to delay embeddings is not justified, including in the otherwise linear-Gaussian case.
issues.title: Overlapping observation windows invalidate the unchanged innovation model
issues.why_classification: The defect is confined to the delay extension and can be addressed by a contained correlated-observation construction or a limited weakening to a heuristic use of windows.
